c.request: Applying a 4.99 cutoff on the payment amount, take the qualifying payments that can be linked to a rental and, through that rental, to an inventory item (leave out payments without such a match). For each rental and store (`inventory.store_id`), total the payment amounts and count the payments. Then for each store, show the store id, the average of those per-rental totals, and the average number of payments per rental (both unrounded, ignoring missing values). Only payments larger than 4.99 are included. Payments of exactly 4.99 are left out.
c.sql: WITH rental_store AS (SELECT p.rental_id, i.store_id, SUM(p.amount) AS total_amount, COUNT(*) AS payment_count FROM payment p JOIN rental r ON r.rental_id = p.rental_id JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id WHERE p.amount > 4.99 GROUP BY p.rental_id, i.store_id) SELECT store_id, AVG(total_amount) AS avg_rental_total, AVG(payment_count) AS avg_payments_per_rental FROM rental_store GROUP BY store_id;

b.request: For payments with amount > 4.99 that join to a rental and then to its inventory item, group by rental_id and inventory.store_id to get each rental's total amount and payment count, then per store_id return the average of those totals and the average payment count, unrounded.
b.sql: SELECT store_id, AVG(total_amount) AS avg_total_amount, AVG(payment_count) AS avg_payment_count FROM (SELECT r.rental_id, i.store_id, SUM(p.amount) AS total_amount, COUNT(*) AS payment_count FROM payment p JOIN rental r ON r.rental_id = p.rental_id JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id WHERE p.amount > 4.99 GROUP BY r.rental_id, i.store_id) t GROUP BY store_id;
b.raw: For payments with amount > 4.99 that join to a rental and then to its inventory item, group by rental_id and inventory.store_id to get each rental's total amount and payment count, then per store_id return the average of those totals and the average payment count, unrounded.

a.request: Take the payments of more than 4.99 that can be linked to a rental and, through that rental, to an inventory item (leave out payments without such a match). For each rental and store (`inventory.store_id`), total the payment amounts and count the payments. Then for each store, show the store id, the average of those per-rental totals, and the average number of payments per rental (both unrounded, ignoring missing values).
a.sql: WITH rental_store AS (SELECT p.rental_id, i.store_id, SUM(p.amount) AS total_amount, COUNT(p.payment_id) AS payment_count FROM payment p JOIN rental r ON r.rental_id = p.rental_id JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id WHERE p.amount > 4.99 GROUP BY p.rental_id, i.store_id) SELECT store_id, AVG(total_amount) AS avg_total_per_rental, AVG(payment_count) AS avg_payments_per_rental FROM rental_store GROUP BY store_id;

d.request: Include only payments with amount > 4.99 (excluding amount = 4.99), join each payment to its rental and then to inventory, group by rental and inventory.store_id to get per-rental totals and payment counts, then per store report store_id, AVG(per-rental total amount), and AVG(per-rental payment count), with unrounded results and NULL-matched rows excluded.
d.sql: SELECT r.store_id, AVG(r.total_amount) AS avg_rental_total, AVG(r.payment_count) AS avg_payment_count FROM (SELECT ra.rental_id, i.store_id, SUM(p.amount) AS total_amount, COUNT(*) AS payment_count FROM payment p JOIN rental ra ON ra.rental_id = p.rental_id JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = ra.inventory_id WHERE p.amount > 4.99 GROUP BY ra.rental_id, i.store_id) r GROUP BY r.store_id ORDER BY r.store_id
